item.title: A 3,000-year-old glimpse into China's Bronze Age technological prowess
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
WUHAN, Sept. 17 (Xinhua) -- China is famous for its ancient inventions: papermaking, printing, gunpowder and the compass. But there is far more to its technological legacy than these. One notable achievement is the Tonglushan ancient copper mining site. More than 3,000 years ago, people in China were already mining and refining high-purity copper on a large scale at this site, a feat that put them some 2,000 years ahead of the rest of the world. Located in Daye, Hubei Province in central China, this site has welcomed more than 20 million visitors since it opened in the 1980s, including tourists from Japan, the Republic of Korea, Europe and Africa. It received official designation as a National Archaeological Site Park in 2025 and is now working toward UNESCO World Heritage status. To further showcase China's ancient industrial achievements to international visitors, a large-screen presentation launched last year features English subtitles alongside Chinese ones, while the park has also opened an educational workshop for visitors from China and abroad. "The site shows that China has long had the capacity to develop advanced technologies independently. It also strengthens our cultural confidence," said Chen Jiayi, a staff member at the site park. In the 21st century, China has once again emerged as a major industrial and technological power -- home to the world's most comprehensive industrial systems and making rapid advances in areas ranging from new-energy vehicles and artificial intelligence to robotics, quantum technology, space exploration and marine science. The Tonglushan site was discovered by chance during mining operations in 1973, and archaeological excavations found that mining and smelting activity there dates back at least to the early years of the Spring and Autumn Period (770 B.C.-476 B.C.). "It confirms that China's Bronze Age civilization followed a complete and independent course of development," Chen said. "Archaeological comparisons show that the copper used in the Bianzhong of Marquis Yi of Zeng, a famous set of bronze chime bells, as well as many other bronze artifacts, came from Tonglushan." Excavations have found that the ancient mine shafts and tunnels at the site total more than 8,000 meters in length, and over 400,000 tonnes of smelting slag have been unearthed so far. Researchers estimate that between 80,000 and 120,000 tonnes of crude copper were produced there over the centuries, enough to cast about 48,000 sets of bronze bells comparable in scale to those of Marquis Yi of Zeng, or a far larger number of ritual vessels and weapons. "Bronze gave physical form to China's long-standing ritual and musical traditions, its social hierarchy, its way of life, and indeed its pluralistic yet unified civilization," Chen said. Ancient craftsmen at this location had already mastered sophisticated mining and smelting techniques. They used bellows-equipped shaft furnaces and two procedures, namely "oxidized ore to copper" and "sulphide ore to matte to copper," thereby precisely controlling furnace temperatures at around 1,200 degrees Celsius. At the time, crude copper reached a purity of 93 percent, while the copper content in slag was just 0.7 percent, which is a level far ahead of the rest of the ancient world, with some techniques approaching near-modern standards. Mining and metallurgical activity at Tonglushan never really stopped, and by the late 19th century it was home to what was then Asia's largest integrated iron and steel enterprise, while production further expanded after the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949. "Today, copper production here has moved into higher-value processing, serving fields such as new-energy vehicles, 5G communications and semiconductor chips," said Pan Xiaojin, mayor of Daye. Daye has also expanded into a range of other industries, including intelligent connected new-energy vehicles, optoelectronic information, hydrogen energy, intelligent robotics, the low-altitude economy and green building materials. "The spirit of craftsmanship, fueled by a drive to grow stronger and tempered through countless trials, continues to inspire us to create new wonders," Pan noted. ■

item.title: Chinese delegation welcomed at Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 17 (Xinhua) --The Chinese delegation was officially welcomed at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Thursday, as athletes and officials gathered at Nagoya Port ahead of the opening ceremony of the continental multi-sport event. The Team Welcome Ceremony, held at the Fuji no Hiroba Athlete Interaction Area in Garden Pier, featured the introduction of delegations, cultural performances, flag-raising and commemorative gift exchanges. Chinese women's basketball players Liu Yutong, Tang Ziting, Sun Yu and Jia Saiqi were among those representing the delegation at Thursday's ceremony. For Liu, the ceremony offered an early taste of the Asian Games experience. She said it was her first time attending such a ceremony and that she was excited about the competition ahead. "We will give our best, stay fully focused and face every opponent with the best possible mindset," she added. The Team Welcome Ceremony runs from Wednesday to Friday, with three sessions each day and three to six delegations taking part in each session. The event is designed to formally welcome teams to the Games and bring athletes together ahead of competition. At the end of Thursday's ceremony, representatives from Team China, Hong Kong and Macao delegations posed for a group photo. Wong Po Kee, head of the delegation of Hong Kong, China, said the three delegations had developed a close bond through years of traveling around the world for competitions. This year's Games will coincide with the Mid-Autumn Festival. Wong said the delegation of Hong Kong, China had prepared festive food and activities in advance, adding that the team was accustomed to celebrating traditional festivals away from home while competing overseas. The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games will officially open on Saturday and run through Oct. 4. ■

item.title: Xinhua Headlines: Beyond expo floor, AI opens new frontiers in China-ASEAN cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
*China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) both aim to expand AI's role in bilateral trade, which exceeded 1 trillion U.S. dollars last year. *In the first seven months of 2026, China-ASEAN trade rose 24.7 percent year on year to 744.41 billion dollars, Chinese customs data show, as AI use expands in marketing, agriculture, logistics and finance. *The distinction between technology that draws a crowd and technology that delivers real value is central to the 23rd China-ASEAN Expo and the China-ASEAN Business and Investment Summit, slated from Sept. 17 to 21 in Nanning, Guangxi's capital. NANNING, Sept. 17 (Xinhua) -- Wei Qiaomei, a Chinese livestreamer, once struggled to grasp what her Thai customers wanted, though she speaks fluent Thai. Once, ahead of her pitch for a portable fan, AI analyzed Thai e-commerce data and popped up two selling points for her: quiet motors and long battery life. The trial has proven rewarding. Her employer, based in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, reported a 300 percent sales jump. "Speaking the language isn't the same as understanding the market," said the 23-year-old, noting that AI had transformed her from a mere translator into a market-savvy presenter. Her story reflects a broader shift in relations between China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), as both sides aim to expand AI's role in bilateral trade, which exceeded 1 trillion U.S. dollars last year. In the first seven months of 2026, China-ASEAN trade rose 24.7 percent year on year to 744.41 billion dollars, Chinese customs data show, as AI use expands in marketing, agriculture, logistics and finance. FROM SHOWCASE TO APPLICATION The distinction between technology that draws a crowd and technology that delivers real value is central to the 23rd China-ASEAN Expo and the China-ASEAN Business and Investment Summit, slated from Sept. 17 to 21 in Nanning, Guangxi's capital. The event brings together more than 3,400 companies, with Timor-Leste attending for the first time as ASEAN's 11th member and an official co-host. The expo's inaugural "AI marketplace" features about 500 products from more than 70 companies across eight categories, such as wearables, health management, and consumer technology, allowing visitors to test and buy items on-site. "Last year, AI was mostly for show. This year, it is driving sales," said Wang Jicai, secretary-general of the China-ASEAN Expo Secretariat. For Wei, the results are clear. Her company trained its model on ASEAN languages, local preferences, and cultural nuances, enabling it to analyze products, process reviews, and draft localized scripts. Livestream hosts then decide when to pivot, how to handle tough questions, and what to emphasize. "AI didn't replace me. It amplified what I could do," Wei said. Beyond the livestream studio, AI applications are being deployed in several ASEAN markets. In Laos and Cambodia, a platform developed by a Guangxi enterprise and local partners uses satellite imagery, drones, and ground sensors to track pests and guide tropical crop cultivation. The system, built with Chinese technology, local field data and training support, has been tested on more than 20,000 mu (about 1,333 hectares) of crops, said project head Wen Biaotang. CROSS-BORDER DEPLOYMENT NARROWS AI DIVIDE In Guangxi's border city Chongzuo, the center for disease control and prevention has partnered with neighboring Vietnamese provinces to deploy a bilingual AI platform for early disease detection. It can slash epidemiological reporting time from four hours to 30 minutes, the project manager said. In Nanning, RunDo, a platform operated by Runjian Co. Ltd., monitors almost 300 megawatts of solar capacity across nearly 3,000 sites in Malaysia remotely, with drones and AI replacing manual inspections. "The platform has boosted maintenance efficiency by over 30 percent, raised power output by up to 5 percent, and cut labor costs by more than 20 percent," said Yang Yexi, marketing manager of the operator's Guangxi branch. Leveraging Nanning's computing infrastructure, ASEAN companies can avoid building large intelligent computing centers and remotely access models and computing power for their business needs, Yang said, whose company has launched more than 80 computing projects across ASEAN. These cases highlight the prerequisites for cross-border AI deployment: computing power, local data, skilled workers, and capable local partners. Guangxi's China-ASEAN Artificial Intelligence Application Cooperation Center has cataloged more than 1,000 potential AI scenarios, opened 279 to developers, set up offices in Vietnam, Laos, and Malaysia, backed more than 30 cross-border projects, and assembled an alliance of 55 companies. To address the low-resource challenge faced by some Southeast Asian languages, a training base in Malaysia has logged more than 1,900 hours of multilingual data annotation, while a six-month regional competition attracted more than 200 teams. Liu Jianmin, a professor at the School of Big Data and Artificial Intelligence of Guangxi University of Finance and Economics, said ASEAN universities, companies, and professionals could contribute to collecting, labeling and updating data if AI models are to work locally. "No matter how accurate a system is, if no one uses it, can afford it, or can keep it running, it remains just an exhibit," Liu said. The challenge is acute for ASEAN's smaller economies. Without collective action, the cost of cybersecurity, data governance, and reliable AI frameworks could deepen an "intelligence divide," said Miguel Marques Goncalves Manetelu, Timor-Leste's minister of transport and communications. FROM MATCHMAKING TO RULE-MAKING Before the expo opened, an AI system had generated more than 8,000 buyer-seller matches and arranged nearly 2,000 face-to-face meetings. According to the summit's organizers, the system provides real-time tariff and compliance guidance during negotiations, and tracks leads after the exhibition. But, it still can not establish cross-border data protocols, guarantee electronic signatures, or assign liability when an algorithm fails. AI can turn industrial expertise into a service that can be sold and delivered over time, said Meng Shuang, an associate professor of international economics at the Central University of Finance and Economics in Beijing. Companies, she said, will increasingly package hardware, software, models, and long-term maintenance, with competitive advantage extending to algorithms, sector expertise, and local operating ability. This evolution has pushed regional trade into more complex territory: data governance, AI service pricing and billing rules, electronic authentication, and intellectual property. "Cross-border data flows are the lifeblood of AI," said ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn, who called for a trusted, secure, and seamless framework for data exchange. The China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol, signed in October 2025, sets out a regional framework covering the digital and green economies, cross-border data flows, personal privacy, digital payments, and AI standards. Standardized electronic authentication, interoperable payments, and joint data frameworks would first benefit sectors such as cross-border e-commerce, smart logistics, and industrial inspection, Meng added. Ge Hongliang, a researcher at the School of Southeast Asian Studies at Guangxi Minzu University, said that cooperation among free-trade zones and ports under the upgraded protocol could support investment, data sharing, and intellectual-property protection. To that end, this year's expo is hosting its first high-level dialogue on aligning Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) and China-ASEAN FTA rules. For livestreamers like Wei, it comes down to knowing which fan feature matters most to a customer hundreds of miles away. ■ (Video reporters: Huang Kaiying and Qin Guanghua; video editors: Zhou Yang and Zhu Cong)

item.title: Xinhua Commentary: Hong Kong's first 5-year blueprint charts clear course for development
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
HONG KONG, Sept. 17 (Xinhua) -- The first five-year plan of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) is of milestone significance in advancing the practice of "one country, two systems" and marks a crucial step for Hong Kong to expedite the transition from stability to prosperity and achieve high-quality development. The guiding document unveiled on Wednesday charts a clear course for Hong Kong's economic and social development from 2026 to 2030. The formulation of the plan reflects a profound shift in Hong Kong's governance approach and development model, demonstrating the notable improvement in the governance capacity of the HKSAR government under "one country, two systems." Built on consensus from all sectors of Hong Kong society, the blueprint will further enhance the HKSAR's governance efficacy, making the development direction clearer, resource allocation more efficient, and social expectations more stable, and providing stronger safeguards for the well-being of its residents and the interests of investors. The plan will consolidate and enhance Hong Kong's status as an international financial, maritime and trade center, and develop the region into an international innovation and technology center and a global hub for high-caliber talent. The blueprint comes as Hong Kong's economic growth gains momentum, with social stability and prosperity providing an indispensable environment and foundation for the city to implement medium- and long-term planning. The Hong Kong society has been calling for a more forward-looking and holistic blueprint for development. One of the underlying principles of the plan is to uphold the two-pronged approach of "effective market" and "capable government." Far from weakening the market, this governance innovation strengthens strategic guidance, unleashes market vitality, and turns institutional advantages into real development gains. It provides Hong Kong with a powerful tool to tackle long-standing deep-seated problems and gives full play to the advantages and vitality of the "one country, two systems" policy. This year marks the start of the national 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), which includes arrangements for promoting the long-term prosperity and stability of the HKSAR and the Macao SAR by supporting the two regions in consolidating and enhancing their competitive advantages, and helping them better integrate into and contribute to the country's overall development. Aligned with the national five-year plan, the HKSAR's blueprint seeks to turn the country's strategic opportunities into the region's development drivers. Hong Kong's plan will leverage the vast mainland market and its comprehensive industrial system, while exerting the city's role as an international platform. It aims to further develop Hong Kong as a gateway and bridge between the country and the world, and as an international metropolis that is more attractive, vibrant and rich in opportunities. A blueprint is only as valuable as its implementation. As long as all sectors of the Hong Kong society fully and faithfully uphold "one country, two systems," adhere to the principle of "patriots administering Hong Kong," maintain and improve its executive-led governance, enable a capable government to deliver results and an effective market to unleash its full potential, and make concerted efforts, the HKSAR will surely translate its grand blueprint into reality. ■

item.title: China urges EU to revise discriminatory clauses in public procurement act proposal
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
BEIJING, Sept. 17 (Xinhua) -- China's Ministry of Commerce on Thursday urged the European Union (EU) to revise discriminatory provisions in the proposed Public Procurement Act, voicing grave concerns over "European preference" provisions that could exclude or restrict third-country companies. He Yadong, spokesperson for the Ministry of Commerce, said at a regular press conference that China has noted the European Commission's release of the act proposal. The proposal introduces "European preference" criteria and requires non-market factors such as security to be included in bid evaluation criteria. This means companies from other countries that do not meet these new conditions could be excluded or face certain restrictions. China is highly concerned about this, He said. China urges the EU side to abide by WTO rules, keep its market open, and revise the discriminatory clauses in the proposal to create a fair, transparent and non-discriminatory business environment for enterprises investing and operating in Europe, the spokesperson said. China will closely monitor the EU's legislative process and assess the relevant impact in a timely manner, He added. ■

item.title: China pushes BeiDou navigation system deeper into global markets
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
CHANGSHA, Sept. 17 (Xinhua) -- China is advancing its BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) deeper into global markets, unveiling new products, technologies and applications at a summit in central China this week, as it seeks to position the system as a shared global service. At the 5th International Summit on BDS Applications held in Zhuzhou, Hunan Province, an international cooperation and innovation base for BeiDou applications was formally inaugurated, with plans to build a series of flagship overseas application demonstration projects and gradually construct a cooperation framework linking China's BeiDou industry with international markets. China has been steadily advancing the overseas rollout of BeiDou technology, products, standards and services, integrating the system into global infrastructure and serving economic and social development in Belt and Road countries. A report on BeiDou industry development released at the summit said that since completing global networking in 2020, the system's global service capabilities have continued to strengthen, with the foundation in place to provide stable, reliable and continuous services worldwide. BeiDou's capabilities in positioning, navigation, timing and short-message communication have continued to improve, reinforcing its global expansion in high-precision applications such as transportation, agriculture, marine fisheries and emergency rescue, according to the report. BeiDou has been fully incorporated into the standards systems of 11 international organizations, including the International Civil Aviation Organization, the International Maritime Organization and COSPAS-SARSAT, an international satellite system for search and rescue, covering core areas like civil aviation, maritime affairs and mobile communications. Zhang Junping, a Hunan provincial government official overseeing business services, said BeiDou is now one of four global satellite navigation systems recognized by the United Nations, with related products exported to more than 140 countries and regions. In Belt and Road countries, BeiDou applications and products account for 58 percent of the market, he noted. Zhang cited projects ranging from smart port operations at Peru's Chancay port to BeiDou monitoring on the China-Maldives Friendship Bridge, and from precision agriculture in Laos to taxi dispatch in Cambodia. Experts at the summit said satellite navigation is not a zero-sum game, and that BeiDou is willing to be compatible and interoperable with other global navigation systems to jointly build global spatial-temporal infrastructure. Demonstration projects have already been implemented in multiple African and Southeast Asian countries for land surveying, disaster monitoring and fisheries management. Myo Thant, deputy director general of the Myanmar Space Agency, said there is considerable potential for BeiDou applications in Myanmar, particularly in high-precision positioning, transportation, agriculture, surveying and mapping, and disaster management. "Myanmar is keen to deepen practical cooperation with China and other stakeholders in technical standards, testing and certification, professional training, capacity building, technology transfer and the development of practical BeiDou application projects," Thant added. BeiDou now provides signal coverage to over 200 countries and regions. Its international promotion is entering a key transition period from broad expansion to deeper value creation, and from product exports to ecosystem building, the report said. ■

item.title: China unveils crop farming plan to boost grain capacity by 2030
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
BEIJING, Sept. 17 (Xinhua) -- China will steadily enhance its comprehensive grain production capacity by 2030 and hold the bottom line of basic self-sufficiency in grains and absolute security in staple foods, according to the national crop farming development plan for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) released by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs. Under the plan, by 2030 China will consolidate and enhance the production capacity of soybeans, oilseeds, cotton and sugar crops to maintain a reasonable level of self-sufficiency, and ensure balanced, diverse and safe supplies of vegetables, fruits and tea. The plan also sets targeted measures for different crops and regions. Placing strong emphasis on the green transition, the plan calls for agricultural water conservation and more meticulous use of fertilizer and pesticides. It also highlights the leading role of new quality productive forces in agriculture, including breeding and promoting breakthrough varieties and applying intelligent machinery. Technology already contributes more than 64 percent to China's agricultural output growth. The crop farming plan is aligned with the plan to accelerate agricultural and rural modernization during the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) period, which sets a target of increasing the country's comprehensive grain production capacity to 1.45 trillion jin (about 725 million tonnes) by 2030. "The 15th Five-Year Plan period is critical for basically achieving agricultural and rural modernization," said Zhao Changbao, director of the Rural Economy Research Center of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, in a recent article. "Continuously raising the land output rate, resource utilization rate and labor productivity is an inevitable choice for responding to changes at home and abroad, consolidating the foundation of agricultural development and safeguarding national food security," he said. Zhao noted that the plan dovetails with the requirement of the plan to accelerate agricultural and rural modernization during the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) period to boost output and production capacity, production and ecology, and output and income simultaneously. China's grain security foundation has continued to strengthen. The country's grain output reached about 714.9 million tonnes in 2025, marking the second straight year with grain output above 700 million tonnes. The plan comes as global food security faces mounting headwinds. The 2026 State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World report, released in July by five United Nations specialized agencies, estimated that about 645 million people, or 7.8 percent of the global population, were affected by hunger in 2025. China feeds nearly 20 percent of the world's population with less than 9 percent of its arable land, and has kept its grain self-sufficiency rate at a high level. ■

item.title: Xi stresses sustained efforts to expand, strengthen advanced manufacturing
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
BEIJING, Sept. 17 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged sustained efforts to expand and strengthen advanced manufacturing to provide strong support for advancing Chinese modernization. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction, which was conveyed at a national conference on advanced manufacturing held in Beijing on Wednesday and Thursday. Efforts should be made to ensure both high-quality development and greater security, pursue smart, green and integrated development, and make the country's industrial chains more self-supporting and risk-resilient, Xi stressed. He emphasized the need to accelerate the development of a modernized industrial system with advanced manufacturing as the backbone, and reinforce the foundations of the real economy. Chinese Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, delivers a speech at a national conference on advanced manufacturing held in Beijing, capital of China. The national conference on advanced manufacturing was held in Beijing on Wednesday and Thursday. An instruction of Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, was conveyed during the conference. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen) Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, delivered a speech at the conference. Xi's important instructions provide essential guidance for developing advanced manufacturing, Li said, noting that China must treat developing advanced manufacturing as a major strategic task, and press steadily to boost its strength in manufacturing. Li stressed that next-generation intelligent manufacturing should serve as the primary direction, with greater emphasis on digital and intelligent empowerment, high-end manufacturing and self-reliance, green and low-carbon development, and cross-sector integration. Efforts should be made to continuously strengthen the innovation capacity, competitiveness and overall strength of advanced manufacturing, Li said. Li called for deepening the "AI plus manufacturing" initiative, stepping up guidance and support for enterprises' digital and intelligent transformation, and consolidating the foundation of intelligent software and hardware. China should also advance the deep integration of advanced manufacturing and modern services, foster service-oriented manufacturing, and cultivate advanced manufacturing clusters according to local conditions. Chinese Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, delivers a concluding speech at a national conference on advanced manufacturing held in Beijing, capital of China. The national conference on advanced manufacturing was held in Beijing on Wednesday and Thursday. An instruction of Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, was conveyed during the conference. (Xinhua/Gao Jie) In his concluding speech, Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing, also a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, said China should further implement the initiative for high-quality development of key industrial chains, accelerate the building of a high-quality standards system, continue to address disorderly and irrational competition, and create a sound ecosystem for advanced manufacturing. ■
